title: Latest TicWatch Pro does not work reliably, as a Standalone Collector
body:
Latest TicWatch Pro does not work reliably, as a Standalone Collector

https://www.facebook.com/groups/xDripG5/permalink/3047785118628296/

Folks,

Despite much chatter in the forums, I have been unable to get TicWatch Pro working as a stand-alone collector.

I personally, had no success at all the with 31 January version of xDrip+. I’ve had more success with 18 May version of xDrip+. However, Ticwatch Pro only stays running in standalone mode for between 2 to 12 hours, at best. Then it simply stops collecting. It always loses connection overnight.  If I then stop collecting wait 10 minutes and restart collecting on the watch it will resume again.

Here is my configuration.
Samsung S9 (SM-G960F), running Android OS version 9
xDrip+ 2019/01/31 (c/o ParapenT1sta) and tried 2019/05/18 (c/o David Potter)
MM1
Libre sensor 14 day UK version
TicWatchPro (recently purchased)
WearOS 2.28

I’ve tried two versions of xDrip+ the people have suggested work for them xDrip+ 2019/01/31 (c/o ParapenT1sta) and 2019/05/18 (c/o David Potter). 

I have followed the ideas discussed in problem report 840.
https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/issues/840

I have tried, IDEA NO 1, these ideas from David (Thank you, David)
“ ……………….With the help of Kirsten Verity Firefly's post in the miaomiao facebook group, I may have solved my issue. Hopefully this will help others.
I think the whole problem is competing Bluetooth.
I don't need Bluetooth on my Android for anything.
Here's what I did and again, Thanks are to Kirsten
1.	Check Force Collector on the phone
2.	Turn Bluetooth off on the phone
3.	wait and see what happens
4.	if you lose signal tap the three vertical dots on the watch
5.	Restart the Collector from the watch
6.	I have both my phone and watch connected to my work and home wifi.
When I got to work the value on the phone had a line through it, as expected and the watch was working fine. Once the watch and phone reconnected to my work wifi everything was back to normal. Same readings on both and phone is uploading to Nightscout :-)
Tip: On the watch under accessibility there is a magnification option. When you tap the screen 3x it enlarges that area. It also brings the area to the centre of the watchface. Tap the 3 dots 3 times and they will enlarge in the centre of the watchface. Tap once more and the menu will open up where you can restart the collector.”

I have tried, IDEA NO 2, these ideas are also from David (Again, Thank you David)
“…………Okay so another update which hopefully will help some. Thank you to Andrew Cruikshank
My Ticwatch died and I was back to square one. After following the steps below I have both my Ticwatch Pro and my daughter’s Fossil Gen4 back up and running. The Fossil Gen4 had not worked since January.
1.	get Xdrip running on both the watch and phone with Force Collector unchecked
2.	check Force Collector only on the watch. The phone should vibrate or sound with a notification
3.	on the watch press the 3 vertical dots and select restart Collector
4.	I went into Bluetooth on the watch and miaomiao was showing as available. I tapped it and it came up with “pairing” but then showed as available again.
After this watch was working standalone
Steps 3/4 can be reversed. I'm not 100% certain they are both necessary, but I do know that both watches are working again standalone with Xdrip. Very happy   and thanks to Andrew….”

I have tried, IDEA NO 3, these ideas are from ParapenT1sta. Namely his Portugese tutorial. With no success. Appreciate your efforts producing this Parapen.

I appreciate all the help on the forums I’ve had and also for the sterling work carried out by the developers.

Any thoughts, or ideas, please?

Thank you
•	
Kwis Jones Mine's OK I use may xdrip as well. So far since may only 2 disconnections and restarted tic watch and reconnected automatically. I don't use it as a standalone, I can't see the point of that. It's the collector so when it's in range it sends all the data to my phone which sends it all to nightscout. But I'm not attached to my phone
o	Chris Carter Kwis Jones thank you for your input, Chris

•	Andrew Cruikshank Have you updated the wear OS to the most recent version, my watch is running wear OS 2.9. And except of the odd connection issues my TicPro runs standalone fine, using the methods you listed above.
o	Chris Carter Andrew Cruikshank Hi Andrew, thank you for your reply. Could I plse ask what version of xDrip plus you are using? Thank you Chris
o	Andrew Cruikshank Not sure I’ll check when I get home and let you know.
o	Andrew Cruikshank Chris Carter version 14fecb8-2019.01.10
o	Chris Carter Andrew Cruikshank Cheers Andrew, I will try this version

•	Mike Simmons I use a ticwatch E2. I have to turn bluetooth off on the phone, then go to xdrip settings on the watch and turn on enable wear collection and force wear collection, then I go to bluetooth settings on the watch and scan for the miaomiao. Tap connect and it will say pairing and then quickly back to available. As long as it says pairing even if it is a fraction of a second it then works standalone. When I want to go back to my phone I turn off enable wear collection and force wear collection on the watch, put the watch in airplane mode and then turn bluetooth back on on the phone and reconnect. A bit involved but it seems to work
o	Chris Carter Mike Simmons thank you Mike for the information. I will try it out.
